title: Linear lift of free restriction and equivariant Yoneda descent
statement:
Work in compatible universes and small skeletons [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $J$ be a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, let $P$ be the profinite site with finite jointly surjective covers [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and let $P_J$ have profinite continuous left $J$-spaces, continuous equivariant maps and finite jointly surjective covers [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $H(S)=J\times S$ with left translation on $J$, and $tS=S$ with trivial action [def-sfb-profinite-action-parameters]. Put $\mathscr E=\operatorname{Sh}(P)$ and let $\mathscr E^{\underline J}$ be the category of internal actions: a sheaf $X$ with a natural unital associative action $C(S,J)\times X(S)\to X(S)$ [lem-sfb-action-topos-geometric-restriction]. Write $h_T(S)=C(S,T)$, with the induced action when $T\in P_J$. Let $R$ be a commutative condensed ring, with trivial $\underline J$-action. Use $\Phi$, $G$, $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ with the formulas of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation, lem-sfb-profinite-action-free-restriction, lem-sfb-profinite-action-cech-recovery]. Give
$$\mathcal R_J(T)=Q_R(T)\subseteq R(T)$$
the inherited ring operations and restrictions. This is a sheaf of commutative rings on $P_J$. There is a canonical ring isomorphism $e_{R,S}:\mathcal R_J(H(S))\xrightarrow{\sim}R(S)$ given by restriction to $(1,s)$, natural in $S$, and every $r_g$ induces the identity under it. For an internal $R$-module $N$ with natural $R(S)$-linear $\underline J$-action [def-sfb-condensed-action-module, sk-def-sfb-module-objects], the subsets
$$\Phi_R(N)(T)=Q_N(T)\subseteq N(T)$$
are closed under addition, negatives and pointwise multiplication by $\mathcal R_J(T)$, and form a sheaf of $\mathcal R_J$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An equivariant linear map acts by its restriction to these subsets. Conversely, for any sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal R_J$-modules, the section groups $G_R(M)(S)=M(H(S))$ have $R(S)$-module structures via $e_{R,S}$, semilinear restriction maps along $H(f)$, and $R(S)$-linear actions $M(r_g)$. They reconstruct an internal $R$-module with $\underline J$-action, with the identical underlying section modules and restrictions of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. These assignments define additive functors $\Phi_R$ and $G_R$. For every $M$, $M(a_T)$ identifies $M(T)$ linearly with $Q_{G_R(M)}(T)$ over $\mathcal R_J(T)$, where this ring acts through its inclusion into $R(T)$. For every $N$, evaluation $e_{N,S}$ is $R(S)$-linear. Consequently $\eta_M$ and $\epsilon_N$ are natural linear isomorphisms for these functors.

proof.text: Use the small skeleton and coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. On the profinite site with abelian coefficients, [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] supplies abelian sheafification and the sheafified objectwise tensor. The stability of sheafification-isomorphisms under objectwise tensor in [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-local-iso] is precisely the monoidal-local-equivalence hypothesis needed for [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Thus that equivalence applies to $P$; no claim about tensoring arbitrary local equivalences is left implicit.

proof.text: For trivially acted-on $R$, $Q_R(T)$ is the equalizer of the ring homomorphisms $R(\alpha_T),R(\pi_T):R(T)\to R(J\times T)$. It contains $0,1$ and is closed under addition, negatives and multiplication. Restrictions along equivariant maps preserve this equation. Its underlying set presheaf is the sheaf $\Phi(R)$ of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation], hence these operations make it a ring sheaf. Write $p_S:H(S)\to S$ for projection of underlying spaces and $\iota_S(s)=(1,s)$. The same node gives the bijection $e_{R,S}=\iota_S^*$ and, by its inverse formula with trivial action, $e_{R,S}^{-1}(a)=p_S^*a$. Evaluation is a ring homomorphism, hence a ring isomorphism. For $f:V\to S$, $p_SH(f)=fp_V$, giving naturality. Also $p_Sr_g=p_S$, so $\mathcal R_J(r_g)p_S^*a=p_S^*a$ for every $a$; consequently every right translation is the identity on coefficients under $e_R$.

proof.text:
Use the unchanged section modules of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Put $A=N(\alpha_T)$, $B=N(\pi_T)$ and $\rho(x)=\gamma\cdot x$ on $N(J\times T)$. The action is linear by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module], so $A,B,\rho$ are additive. For $x,y\in Q_N(T)$, $A(x+y)=\rho B(x)+\rho B(y)=\rho B(x+y)$ and $A(-x)=\rho B(-x)$. For $a\in Q_R(T)$ and $x\in Q_N(T)$, semilinearity of restrictions and linearity of $\rho$ give
$$A(ax)=R(\alpha_T)(a)\rho B(x)=R(\pi_T)(a)\rho B(x)=\rho B(ax).$$
Thus $Q_N(T)$ is a module over $Q_R(T)$ with the inherited operations; all module identities are those in $N(T)$. Equivariant restrictions preserve these subsets and are semilinear. The underlying sets are already the sheaf $\Phi(N)$ by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation], so these are sheaves of modules in the explicit sense of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: For an equivariant linear $v:N\to N'$, equivariance and naturality send the defining equation of $Q_N(T)$ to that of $Q_{N'}(T)$. By [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation] the resulting map is exactly $v_T$ restricted to the subset. It is $Q_R(T)$-linear. Identities and composites restrict to identities and composites. Since $(v+w)_T(x)=v_T(x)+w_T(x)$ on the very same subsets, $\Phi_R(v+w)=\Phi_R(v)+\Phi_R(w)$ and $\Phi_R(0)=0$. This proves the claimed additive functor $\Phi_R$.

proof.text:
For a module sheaf $M$ define $G_R(M)(S)=M(H(S))$ and $a\cdot x=(p_S^*a)x$ for $a\in R(S)$. Step 2 says $p_S^*a=e_{R,S}^{-1}(a)$ in $\mathcal R_J(H(S))$, so this is the required module structure. For $f:V\to S$, the module-sheaf restriction axiom [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] gives
$$M(H(f))((p_S^*a)x)=(p_V^*R(f)(a))M(H(f))(x).$$
The same axiom and step 2 give $M(r_g)((p_S^*a)x)=(p_S^*a)M(r_g)(x)$, proving $R(S)$-linearity of each action operator. The underlying set presheaf is a sheaf and these operators form a natural unital associative left action by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-free-restriction]. Thus the additive groups with these restrictions are an abelian sheaf, and the displayed scalar compatibility makes it a sectionwise $R$-module sheaf.

proof.text: Apply [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence], whose hypotheses were checked in step 1, in the reverse direction to the sectionwise $R$-module sheaf of step 5. It reconstructs an internal module with the identical section groups and restrictions. Naturality and sectionwise linearity of the action give exactly the action-module datum of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. For a module-sheaf morphism $v:M\to M'$, take $G_R(v)_S=v_{H(S)}$. Its $\mathcal R_J(H(S))$-linearity implies $R(S)$-linearity, and naturality at $r_g$ gives equivariance. The underlying natural equivariant map is the one in [lem-sfb-profinite-action-free-restriction]. Identities, composition, zero and addition are preserved because their components are the identical section maps. This defines the additive functor $G_R$.

proof.text:
For $a\in\mathcal R_J(T)$ the coefficient of $M(a_T)$, expressed in $R(T)$, is
$$e_{R,T}(\mathcal R_J(a_T)a)=\iota_T^*R(a_T)a=R(a_T\iota_T)a=a,$$
since $a_T\iota_T=\operatorname{id}_T$. This proves precisely the claimed inclusion of the scalar ring into $R(T)$, rather than an arbitrary coefficient identification. By the module-sheaf restriction axiom [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category],
$$M(a_T)(am)=a\,M(a_T)(m),$$
with the right hand side using the $R(T)$-structure on $G_R(M)(T)$. The bijection onto $Q_{G_R(M)}(T)$ and its naturality are the statements of [lem-sfb-profinite-action-cech-recovery]. Thus the bijection is additive and $\mathcal R_J(T)$-linear; its inverse is linear as well, by applying its injective forward map to the addition and scalar identities. These are the components of $\eta_M$.

proof.text:
For $N$, evaluation on free parameters is restriction $e_{N,S}=\iota_S^*$ on $Q_N(H(S))$ by [lem-sfb-profinite-action-yoneda-free-evaluation]. For $a\in R(S)$ and $x\in Q_N(H(S))$ its linearity is the explicit identity
$$\iota_S^*((p_S^*a)x)=\iota_S^*p_S^*(a)\,\iota_S^*x=a\,\iota_S^*x.$$
It also preserves addition, since the restriction of a section module is additive [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Its bijectivity is free evaluation, and [lem-sfb-profinite-action-cech-recovery] supplies naturality in parameters and in $N$, and intertwining of all family actions $r_g$. Hence these maps are the equivariant natural linear isomorphism $\epsilon_N:G_R\Phi_R(N)\to N$.

proof.text: The naturality equations for $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ in [lem-sfb-profinite-action-cech-recovery] concern exactly the underlying section maps used here. By steps 7 and 8 every component is linear, and inverse bijections are linear by the injectivity argument of step 7. Thus the same equations hold in the module categories, completing both natural linear isomorphisms for the additive functors constructed in steps 4 and 6.
